Respiratory Illness Outbreak Strains Ghana’s Electric Utilities Workforce

A sudden outbreak of respiratory illness has disrupted operations at multiple electric utilities sites across Ghana, causing staff shortages and delays in ongoing maintenance and grid upgrade projects. The outbreak, first reported last week among line workers at the Volta Power Consortium’s Accra substation, has now affected at least four additional facilities operated by different utilities, according to the Ghana Energy Workers’ Association (GEWA).

As of Tuesday, more than 80 employees across the sector have been diagnosed with the illness, described by local health officials as presenting with fever, cough, and shortness of breath. “We are working closely with health authorities to contain the situation, but the impact on crew availability is significant,” said Emmanuel Korsah, Operations Director at SunGrid Electric, one of the affected utilities. “There are delays in scheduled maintenance, and some minor faults are taking longer to resolve.”

The Ministry of Energy has acknowledged the risk to grid reliability if the outbreak continues. “We have asked utilities to activate contingency staffing and limit non-essential site visits,” said Deputy Minister Evelyn K. Owusu. “Our priority is the health of workers and the uninterrupted supply of power.”

Industry analysts warn that extended absenteeism could hinder ongoing infrastructure upgrades, particularly in the Greater Accra and Ashanti regions. “This comes at a critical time for the sector, with several grid expansion projects underway,” noted Kwame Mensah, a senior analyst at Ghana Power Review.

GEWA has urged all member utilities to enhance safety protocols and provide protective equipment. The union is also calling for clear communication and support for affected workers and their families as the situation develops.
